[quote=nordiheim;60453738][spoiler=Immediate retreat][b][u]Eastern Dragon[/u][/b]
As the Nordiheimian navy ships was guarding the saving the desperate Argossian tribal people on the two lower island the stealth fighters flying south-eastward from the islands would dedect someting horrible, a large amount of aircraft with a navy task force following them, and some of those plains readings mached the now known F-15 of Pantagruel, they turned around immediatly and warned the fleet about this.

The admiral on the cruiser could only see one smart course of action, it seemed that Pantagruel had awakened like an eastern dragon and Nordiheim had in either foolishness or overconfidence been caught with insuficient intell, someting he would have to assume that Pantagruel had not, an immidiate withdrawl.
They still had enough time to escape back to the closest Nordiheimian military base on its eastmost island in the Argossian strait, tough they would need to wether the storm of the aircraft.

The whole fleet would sett sail westward at full speed with, their AA defences at full readiness and the Skjoeldr Combat System on line, all systems would have to work together if they were to avoid as much danger as possible, the aircraft that was there or close would provide aditional defence with the 2 stealth observation UAVs staing on the flanks to provide some extra vision.
The civilan ships with the Argossians that they could save would sail sepperate of them on a more south-west direction directly to Ostland.
Hopefully the PDF was not interested in them, but the navy ships.
A urgent message was sendt to HQ about the situation.
------------------------------------------------------------------
[u]HQ[/u]
HQ would go into immidiate action when they recived the news, all navy and air assets that could was ordered to travel from the mainland and meet up with the fleeing force at the designated island to create a force that could meet the PDF if hard came to hard, among it 2 Tyr-Class Cruisers, AWAC and Electronic warfare assets being among the most important tings that would be sendt there.

The council of Nordiheim would start to discus what they might have to do, and how they would react to further news.
------------------------------------------------------------------
[u]The PDF aircrafts attack[/u]
No mather how fast the fleet was there was no way that the air element of the PDF would not cach up, they would engage them with great furry.
The stealth fighters and KJ-6G Kookaburra would fire at them with over the over the horizon missiles to try and dampen their attack before breaking away, while any KJ-5H Cockatoo would try to intercept their missiles with some limited ability.
The AA defences would fire all they had at the mix of anti-ship missiles with some being stoped, but not all could be found in the MALD-J drone swarms interference unfortunatly.
The battleship NN Odin would take 2 hits, one absorbed by its large superstructure while the other would hit its helicopter landing deck taking out 2 of the helicopers there, meanwhile the battleship NN Thor would not be that lucky and would suffer a devestating hits that would make it start sinking rapidly, water gushing inn with almoust no hindrance with how deep on of the hits had gotten.
In adition a partoll boat would also be hit, being compleatly gutted by the hit and disepearing into the sea quickly.

When the Pantagruel aircrafts had done their job the Nordiheimian fleet would continue with full speed, the admiral reporting that the PDF were absolutely seemed to be as prepared as he had feared, together with the losses wich included some of the KJ-5H Cockatoos wich the Pantagruel F-15s had been able to hit despite their best attempts of using flares to avoid their fate.
------------------------------------------------------------------
[u]The councils desicion:[/u]
When the report about the engagement from the PDF aircraft came inn the council of Nordiheim decided that the military had not been prepared enough for Pantagruels responce.
Together with a general lack of information being aquired about that nation and its abilities there was no telling what their full power was, while there was some confidence that they would be able to protect their homeland when everyting arrived back it would most likely cost many good soldiers lives, someting that they would rather avoid.

While the Nordiheim military was getting the defences ready for the worst case scenario the council would send a direct diplomatic message to Pentagruel in the hope to avoid furter escalation and loss of life;
[b]What was its demands for peace?[/b][/spoiler]

[nation]Pantagruel[/nation]
[nation]Shahzada[/nation] rp[/quote]
[pre]POST-BELLUM

Witnessing the emberassing retreat of the Nordiehemian fleet, the Mugunghwa Shield decided to leave them be seeing as they were not a threat to Pantagruel's interests. But their stalking presence hadn't ceased, from the multiple small surveillance drones wizzed into the air, stalking the Nordihimiean fleet from several kilometers afar. The drones kept a constant eye on them, ensuring Nordiheim wasn't bluffing on her commitment. Meanwhile, the remaining F/A-18s banked from their courses towards Astanir, with the UDF emancipated from Nordiheim's blockade they could now return to regular operations. With ISR granted by the E-2D who also analyzed data about the lower islands, the Hornets were now deadset on completely destroying the Argossian militias. Multiple targets were chosen, mainly whatever central command centers and military encroachments the Argossians had left, covered by the toxic gas attacks the UDF had conducted earlier, the Hornets flew confidently knowing manned AA's would have trouble even engaging them considering their situation. Once the Hornets reached within the contested warzone, they released their renowned AGM-65 Mavericks, infamous ground attack missiles known for their surgical precision and destructive capability. The missiles soared across the Astaniran mainland, hugging the terrain as it calculated its course and trajectory, each slight movement fiercly recalculated and inputted into the missiles dataframe. 12 missiles for 12 different targets, each unsuspecting the impending doom. 

On the ground, UDF forces stormed into the vast jungles of the lower islands. After 2 days of blight, the gas had done its job. Argossian positions throne off the rails, now in a position where the UDF could tear it apart piece by piece. The island was divided into multiple zones, where a select army of the UDF was deployed to, specialised for its knowns and unknowns. The UDF was also covered by constant ordnance support from battery pieces that hid at the rear of the frontline, providing the UDF a trump card that could shift any battle in their favour. [/pre]

[b]Table Talks
[/b]
[i]Daesun had recieved Nordiheim's cries for a ceasefire, knowing the nation was no where near being a legitimate threat, Daesun decided to accept their offer and list their demands and grievances. Daesun's demands are as follows;

[list]
[*] All active combat between Nordiheim, the PDF, and the UDF shall cease
[*] Nordiheim will sign a 6 year non-aggression pact with Daesun and a 10 year non-aggression pact with the UDF
[*] Nordiheim will pull out from the Astaniran civil war, and shall bring with it all of its military assets
[*] A prisoners of war exchange shall take place between the UDF and Nordiheim
[*] Nordiheim will forfeit all intel, economic, and military assets about the Argossian militias to the UDF and Daesun
[*] Daesun will pay Nordiheim 500M$ in damages caused by the PDF on Nordiheimian military assets
[*] Nordiheim will recognise the UDF as the sole successor to the Military State of Astanir
[*] Nordiheim will also recognize Daesun's claims to the lower island archipelago
[*] An embassy exchange between Daesun and Nordiheim shall take place

[/list]

Daesun awaits Nordiheim's acceptance of this deal, and an end to the unexcused bloodshed that she has caused. Though one thing is guaranteed, if Nordiheim shows any intent of rejecting the deal, the Eastern Dragon won't hesitate to engrave her annihilation.[/i]

[b][u]The council room in Midgard.[/u][/b]
The council of Nordiheim would look over the terms with heavy hearths, though none as much as minister of war Grand general Thormod Thormodson III, it would be desided that the terms was acceptable considering the foolish orders of the Grand general, wich was the core reason for it all to escalate this far in the first place, no amount of "justification" would realy have avoided this as that was joust not how the world worked despite what some would mean it should.

Thormod knew that being part of the delegation that would sign this treaty, wich would make the demands legal and binding, would proberly be the last ting he would do as the minister of war as there was allready talks among those military officers that had objected to his orders and general strategy from the start that another officer would be more fitting for the position, one that wasn't known for taking chanses or being lax in military doctrin even when it seemed exessive and wastefull.
He might even have to retire in shame, a rather bitter fealing.

[b][i]Diplomatic message to Pantagruel:[/i][/b] Nordiheim would accept the demands, a delegation would be sendt to sign it propperly and bindingly!

[b][u]Orders and a dark message[/u][/b]
Orders was sendt to all forces and agents of Nordiheim in the Astanir theater when the deal was signed, all off them would return home immediatly, submarines would be sendt to extract those in more dangerous areas.

A dark and sad message was also delivered to the Argossian militia, Nordiheim was no longer able to provide them any support of any kind, they had been bested by Pantagruel.
They wished them good luck, for wathever it was worth.
Nordiheim did not expect them to take the news well, most likely they proberly felt somewhat betrayed, but this was joust how life was sometimes.

Nordiheim was out of the Astanir civil war!
-----------------------
Back in Nordiheim the man who would most likely become the next minister of war was allready buisy making a report about the military and certain sections of its command, it would not be mercifull towards that wich he felt was its greatest and most foolish flaws wich would need to be fixed, his ancestors demanded he give his all to do his duty propperly joust as they had done.

A luz filtrou pelo escritório do Primeiro Ministro Gaspar Lourenço de Sousa, o segundo homem mais poderoso no império, atrás somente do imperador,  ele estava sentado em sua cadeira a frente de sua mesa feita com madeira de jacarandá, sentado em sua frente estava o diretor de inteligência  Gaspar Reis, dito como mais inteligente do império, vestindo um termo impecável escuro ele entregou ao ministro uma única folha, parecia, um aviso.
"Veja."
Ele falou entregando os papéis, o ministro os pegou cuidadosamente, e se pôs a ler, o conteúdo era uma série de artigos e fontes que falavam sobre a saúde do imperador em aparente declínio, usando fotos em que ele aparecia publicamente com hematomas nas mãos e, sua falta de aparições publicas nos ultimos 6 meses, causando preocupações quanto a sua saúde, Sousa, um pouco preocupado com as notícias,  olhou para os olhos de Reis, que estava com a cabeça levantada, falando algo para si:
"Seis..."
Ele murmurou, antes de Sousa o questionar o que estava pensando:
"Seis oque, diretor Reis?"
O diretor se recompôs rapidamente, reajustou sua gravata, que já parecia bem arrumada, mas seu perfeccionismo via alguma imperfeição.
"Nada, apenas...devaneando."
Ele tomou um gole de seu café, o qual sempre trazia em uma bolsa separada, e então prosseguiu:
"Como pode ver, ministro de Sousa, parece que o povo está começando a desconfiar da saúde do Imperador, o que é, verdade de fato, como bem sabe, mas..."
Ele hesitou um pouco antes de dizer, pensou consigo mesmo:
"[i]Ah, droga, o povo já sabe, que idéia genial Lourenço de Sousa foi você ter sugerido reduzir as aparições do imperador e ter decidido o esconder por trás daquelas cortinas, GÊNIO tu és.[/i]"
O ministro olhou para Reis confuso com a demora dele, e então questionou sobre:
"Mas...?"
Ele gesticulou com as mãos para que Reis prossiga, ele retornou a falar:
"Ah sim, Maciel não conseguirá prolongar a vida do imperador por mais tempo como sabemos, e o herdeiro não estará pronto para herdar o império [i]ainda."[/i]
Ele lançou um longo gole de seu café antes de continuar:
"Maciel é um talento, mas não fazedor de milagres, o menino é talentoso, e inteligente, mas governar [i] Bravanor?[/i]"
O ministro se virou bruscamente para deixar para a janela, ela iluminando suavemente seus olhos, ele falou:
"Há urubus espreitando o garoto, a doença do imperador só os permite mais e mais de quererem influenciar e terem controle, famílias como os Caetano, Bráv, mesmo Corte-Real, poucos parecem não querer, eu sou um deles..."
Gaspar Reis então notou rapidamente o que ele estava se referindo, de fato se o imperador morresse, a regência seria uma disputa pelo controle do príncipe, ele então falou:
"Precisamos, de um plano, e impedir que tais tolas famílias abusem disso...eu tenho uma ideia."
Sousa pareceu curioso com a proposta, se virou de volta, inclinando se a frente novamente, encarando o diretor, franzindo a testa perguntou:
"Pois então explique."
Reis sorriu, satisfeito com a reação do ministro, e começou:
"Na frente pública."
Ele começou a contar com os dedos em gestos:
"O imperador deverá fazer uma aparição, breve, mas que demonstre força e não fraqueza, no balcão do Palácio da Fênix."
Ele olhou para cima em um suspiro longo:
"O imperador não precisará falar, apenas acenar, e mostrar que está saudável, o príncipe poderá falar, um discurso breve, acalmará os boatos e talvez até reduza os urubus no palácio."
Soares teve um vislumbre de esperança e satisfação pela astúcia do Diretor, porém, questionou:
"Mas , e quanto a frente privada, excelência?"
"Ah sim, quanto a isso..."
Ele tomou um gole de seu café, sorriu sutilmente e continuou:
"O príncipe precisará de alguém para o...cercar, não será uma presa fácil..."
"O capitão Maciel?"
O ministro sugeriu, mas logo Reis retrucou :
"Não um soldado, nem um feiticeiro, um [i]assessor[/i], uma pessoa que possa o ensinar a arte de governar,  instruir-lo na corte e história, alguém que possa o proteger e identificar traidores..."
Sousa estreitou os olhos, pensando no nome, embora ele próprio já soubesse da resposta, ele estava pensando em alguém para ser um tutor, talvez o mais habilidoso da história recente, Reis então por fim falou:
"Quem mais poderia proteger o herdeiro das sombras...se não alguém que já trabalha com elas, e conhece todos segredos que...essas sombras escondem?"
Ele lançou um sorriso raro e largo, não precisava de respostas, ele já sabia da resposta, aquele era...o [b]Diretor Gaspar Reis.[/b], Sousa olhou para Reis antes do mesmo sair do escritório em passos rápidos olhando para seu relógio, Sousa murmurou:
"Você mesmo...astuto Reis...."
--------------------
Light filtered into the office of Prime Minister Gaspar Lourenço de Sousa, the second most powerful man in the empire, second only to the emperor. He sat in his chair at his rosewood desk. Sitting across from him was the director of intelligence, Gaspar Reis, said to be the most intelligent in the empire. Dressed in an impeccably dark suit, he handed the minister a single sheet of paper, seemingly a warning.
"Look," he said, handing over the papers. The minister took them carefully and began reading. The contents were a series of articles and sources discussing the emperor's apparently declining health, using photos of him appearing publicly with bruises on his hands. His lack of public appearances in the last six months had raised concerns about his health. Sousa, somewhat concerned by the news, looked into Reis's eyes. Reis's head was raised, saying something to himself:
"Six..."
He murmured, before Sousa asked him what he was thinking:
"Six what, Director Reis?" The director quickly composed himself, readjusting his tie, which already seemed well-groomed, but his perfectionism revealed some imperfection.
"Nothing, just...daydreaming."
He took a sip of his coffee, which he always carried in a separate bag, and then continued:
"As you can see, Minister de Sousa, it seems the people are beginning to suspect the Emperor's health, which is true, as you well know, but..."
He hesitated a moment before saying, thinking to himself:
"[i]Oh, damn, the people already know, what a brilliant idea Lourenço de Sousa was, you suggesting reducing the Emperor's appearances and deciding to hide him behind those curtains, you are a GENIUS."
The minister looked at Reis, confused by his delay, and then asked:
"But...?"
He gestured with his hands for Reis to continue, then resumed speaking:
"Ah yes, Maciel won't be able to prolong the emperor's life any longer as we know, and the heir won't be ready to inherit the empire yet."
He took a long sip of his coffee before continuing:
"Maciel is talented, but not a miracle worker. The boy is talented and intelligent, but ruling Bravanor?"
The minister turned abruptly to face the window, her eyes gently lighting up. He spoke:
"There are vultures stalking the boy. The emperor's illness only allows them to increasingly seek influence and control. Families like the Caetanos, Brávs, even Corte-Reals, few seem to be unwilling. I am one of them..."
Gaspar Reis then quickly realized what he was referring to. Indeed, if the emperor died, the regency would be a contest for control of the prince. He then He said:
"We need a plan to stop those foolish families from abusing this... I have an idea."
Sousa seemed curious about the proposal. He turned back, leaning forward again, facing the director. Frowning, he asked:
"Then explain."
Reis smiled, satisfied with the minister's reaction, and began:
"On the public front."
He began counting off gestures with his fingers:
"The emperor must make an appearance, brief, but demonstrating strength and not weakness, on the balcony of the Phoenix Palace."
He looked up with a long sigh:
"The emperor won't need to speak, just nod and show that he is healthy. The prince can speak. A brief speech will calm the rumors and perhaps even reduce the vultures in the palace."
Soares felt a glimmer of hope and satisfaction at the director's cunning, but asked:
"But what about the private front, your excellency?"
"Ah, yes, about that..."
He took a sip of his coffee, smiled subtly, and continued:
"The prince will need someone to... surround him; he won't be easy prey..."
"Captain Maciel?"
The minister suggested, but Reis quickly retorted:
"Not a soldier, nor a sorcerer, an advisor, someone who can teach him the art of governing, instruct him in court and history, someone who can protect him and identify traitors..."
Sousa narrowed his eyes, considering the name. Although he already knew the answer, he was thinking of someone to be a tutor, perhaps the most skilled in recent history. Reis finally spoke:
"Who else could protect the heir of the shadows...if not someone who already works with them, and knows all the secrets that...these shadows hide?"
He gave a rare, wide smile. He didn't need answers, he already knew the answer, that was... [b]Director Gaspar Reis.[/b], Sousa looked at Reis before he left the office with quick steps, looking at his watch. Sousa murmured:
"Y....yourself... A well made move.... Reis...."
[/Spoiler][/quote]
[Spoiler=2019-Alteza...?]
2019, Pampas.
"Vossa alteza, principe Leo..."
Maciel olhou aos arredores, o campo era grande, poderia estar em qualquer lugar, o imperador havia decidido tomar algumas férias e deixaria o estado nas mãos do Primeiro Ministro, enquanto majestade não estivesse presente, Maciel era quem deveria cuidar do príncipe, mas, alteza era uma criança um tanto ligeira, é fácil de se perder, os pampas eram planos, o que permitia uma criança correr livremente, e misturada com a vontade de explorar livre dos olhos da Guarda De Honra...
.
O príncipe :
O príncipe, então uma simples criança que completaria 10 anos ainda esse ano, estava vagando pelo campo, ele parecia despreocupado com qualquer coisa, e apreciava a natureza...
"Olha só, um garotinho rico vagando...imagino quanto nos pagariam se nos..."
Dois cangaceiros, vestidos em um poncho e bombacha, com um chapéu de aba larga e lenço branco no pescoço, eles apontaram duas facas para vossa alteza e disseram:
"Você aí, parado, pirralho."
Um deles sorriu com certa malícia em seus olhos, e então apontou para um cavalo marrom próximo.
"Só siga o que nós..."
Apesar do aviso, Leo pareceu irreverente quanto a isso, de fato, ignorou e passou no meio deles caminhando, como se eles nem existissem, ele sussurrou, inaudível:
"...esses Cangaceiros fedem a álcool..."
Os dois olharam com incredulidade para o garoto, ofendidos obviamente, e então um colocou o pé na frente do caminho do príncipe, que tropeçou no chão, caindo de cara na grama, eles sorriram.
"Pare de falar baboseiras, seu pai certamente nos dará uma bela recompensa pelo seu resgate."
O outro cangaceiro então bateu no ombro do companheiro, com um tom meio de pressa:
"Tsc, vamos logo Uéton."
O companheiro porém, não se importou, ao invés disso, ele levantou o príncipe pelo punho agarrando com um agarrão sujo, o príncipe parecia, assustado, mas tentava parecer forte mesmo assim.
"Bah, mas vamos lá Garrucha, só dessa vez."
O outro apenas cobre o rosto com a mão, fingindo hesitação, mas então solta uma risada:
"Gegegeheh, vamos lá então ensinar pra esse piá aí então."
Uéton respondeu com um sorriso, e então jogou o garoto contra a grama com um golpe de seu pulso contra seu rosto, com o príncipe sendo jogado contra a grama...
alguns minutos depois.
Enquanto alteza era erguido pela perna pelos cangaceiros, ele tentando lutar, em vão, se debatendo gritando;
"Eu...eu sou forte! Me larguem seus..."
[b]tack[/b].
Mas um soco, o cangaceiro companheiro do agressor, Uéton, olhou para seu parceiro e disse:
"Chega por hoje Garrucha, vambora logo."
O cangaceiro sorriu, e então levantou o príncipe agarrando pelo pescoço, com o pequeno em lágrimas e o rosto inchado, quando ia se preparar para lançar mais um golpe..
[b]Tick[/b].
Um palito de dente atingiu com precisão em seu rosto, não tinha intenção de machucar, mas distrair, ele largou o príncipe imediatamente, e quando se virou viu Maciel, um homem alto, vestimentas simples, mas chiques para o lugar.
"Você é o pai do garoto? Se quiser-"
Um dos bandidos tentou ameaçar, mas logo Maciel o cortou em sua fala, o tom sereno e calmo, como se não passasse de uma conversa casual:
"Eu só quero o garoto, e que saiam."
Os dois cangaceiros riram, e sacaram revólveres em direção de Alexandre, ele revirou os olhos e disse:
"Muito bem..."

The prince:
The prince, a simple child who would turn ten later that year, wandered through the field, seemingly carefree, taking in the beauty of nature.
Look at that, a rich little boy wandering around I wonder how much we could get if we
Two cangaceiros appeared, wearing ponchos and baggy pants, wide-brimmed hats, and white scarves around their necks. They pointed knives at the boy.
You there! Stop, brat.
One of them grinned with a mischievous glint in his eyes and nodded toward a brown horse nearby.
Just follow our
Leo ignored them completely, strolling right between them as if they didnt exist. He whispered, just quietly enough to be unheard:
these Cangaceiros smell like booze
The two men looked at him in disbelief, clearly offended. One stepped into the boys path, making him trip and fall face-first into the grass. They smirked.
Stop babbling, your father will surely give us a nice reward for rescuing you.
The other tapped his companion impatiently on the shoulder.
Tsk, come on, Uéton.
But Uéton didnt care. Instead, he grabbed the prince by the wrist, a rough grip. The boy looked frightened but tried to stay brave.
Bah, come on, Garrucha, just this once.
The other covered his face, pretending hesitation, then laughed.
Gegegeheh, alright, lets teach this little brat a lesson.
Uéton smiled and swung the boy onto the grass with a quick twist of his wrist.
A few minutes later, the prince was dangling by his leg, struggling and shouting:
IIm strong! Let me go, you
[b]tack[/b].
A punch landed. Uéton looked at his partner.
Enough for today, Garrucha. Lets move.
Garrucha smiled and grabbed the prince by the neck. The boys face was swollen and streaked with tears. Just as he was about to strike again
[b]Tick[/b].
A toothpick struck Garruchas face precisely. It wasnt meant to hurt, only to distract. He instantly released the prince and turned to see Maciela tall man in simple but elegant clothes.
Are you the boys father? If you
One of the bandits tried to threaten him, but Maciel cut him off smoothly, his voice calm as if in casual conversation:
I only want the boy and you two to leave.
The two men laughed and raised their revolvers at Alexandre. He rolled his eyes.
I see..."
Leo lay on the grass, eyes watering, face bruised from the earlier attack. He murmured:
A Alexandre
Then he fainted. Maciel gestured briefly, and the air around him turned sharp like knives, slicing through the bandits weapons. They froze, eyes wide.
Witchcraft! Garrucha, get him! Ill cover the back!
But before they could react, Maciel shaped the sharp air into strong strands that bound the bandits and flung them aside.
He looked down at the heir, exhaling heavily.
Lets go kid."
He plucked a toothpick from his pocket, popped it in his mouth, and seemed to relax. Then he lifted the prince onto his back, still unconscious.
Everything is ok now my lord."
Some time later, with the sun setting and painting the sky orange, the prince awoke. Clinging to the captains neck, trembling, he sobbed:
Maciel
Alexandre didnt respond, just carried him safely, calm and steady, as if he were carrying his own child.
Youre awake..." 
he said in a simple tone.
But the prince didnt answer. He buried his face in the captains shoulder, muffling his sobs on the fabric, holding on tighter.
I just want to be strong, I want I want..."
He repeated it over and over. Maciel didnt reply but gently held his hand, a small gesture of care, speaking not as the emperors sons guardian but as to a fragile child who needed protection:
Yeah...yeah...I know.
